findings.text: The default `Action` that called `helpCommand` was removed and replaced with `CommandNotFound`. `CommandNotFound` only runs for unknown subcommands, so running bare `asdf` with no arguments no longer prints asdf's custom help (version and plugin list). urfave/cli's generic help prints instead. Unknown commands now also go through `CommandNotFound`, which logs the error and exits 1, but the no-argument case regresses.

The error returned by `helpCommand` in `CommandNotFound` is discarded. `helpCommand` calls `cli.OsExiter(1)` itself on failure, so with a non-exiting `OsExiter` (such as one overridden in tests) the flow carries on and exits with 1 anyway. Several other converted sites, such as `failTest` and `installCommand`, also assume `cli.OsExiter` never returns. They fall through to later code if it does return.

0.reason: The patch removes the app-level `Action` that called `helpCommand` and adds only a `CommandNotFound` handler, which never runs when no arguments are given, so bare `asdf` now shows urfave/cli's generic help instead of asdf's custom help with the version and plugin list.

1.reason: `cli.OsExiter` defaults to `os.Exit`, which never returns, and `helpCommand` already exits on its own failure paths, so discarding its error inside `CommandNotFound` has no effect in normal runs; the fall-through only happens under a hypothetical test override and has nothing to do with the env-var reference bug.
